sn46.3:1.1: The “sight of ascetics” was held to be an inspiration that can set one on the path. In the absence of written books, it was also a prerequisite to hearing the teachings ([dn14:2.14.1](), [mn81:6.5](), [sn46.3:1.1](), [an6.30](), [snp2.4:10.2](), [snp4.4:1.1]()).
sn46.3:2.4: Accordingly, the text emphasizes the investigation into the “teachings” that one has heard. The previous discourse emphasized the discernment between right and wrong. Of course, these are never really separate, as the Buddha teaches us to discern what is right and what is wrong ([dn19:7.1]()).
